compensating.why: hop 1 answers whole numbers itself and passes only the other fractions on
hop 3 passes the size of the denominator
hop 4 trims the String the gold returns

ownership_reason: Only the gold writes the String of the fraction; hops 2-4 pass the numerator and the denominator along unchanged and hop 1 only answers a zero numerator with "0". The gold's javadoc promises the string form of the fraction given by its numerator and denominator, which "23" is not for 2/3 (it is the string form of the whole number twenty-three). No one-line change of the two ints above the gold restores the form: the variant gold never writes a separator, so no argument pair yields "2 / 3". The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc ('"num / dem" or just "num" if the denominator is one'); BigFraction.toString, the sibling implementation, writes numerator + " / " + denominator and the numerator alone for a denominator of one; FractionFormat.format and ProperFractionFormat.format write the numerator, " / " and the denominator (FractionFormatTest testFormat "1 / 2" and testFormatImproper "5 / 3", BigFractionFormatTest testFormat "1 / 2").
